plain_language_analysis: Tukea antavan is a workable calque of supportive but slightly stiff. Tunnusmerkkityökalu is an opaque compound that ordinary users are unlikely to parse as a named indicators tool.
terminology_analysis: Indicators (plural) is collapsed into a singular tunnusmerkki-compound. Tunnusmerkki is closer to hallmark than to SPICT's checklist indicators; palliatiivisen hoidon is the expected Finnish for palliative care and is not approved project terminology.
semantic_risk_analysis: The tool still reads as a supportive-and-palliative-care instrument; no negation, agency or degree shift.
backtranslation_signal: BT returns indicator tool (singular), reflecting the Finnish compound rather than English Indicators Tool. Diagnostic of wording stiffness, not a hidden meaning reversal.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Tukea antavan ja palliatiivisen hoidon tunnusmerkkien työkalu (SPICT-4ALL-……)
rationale: Title meaning is recognisable, but the compound is unnatural Finnish and slightly miscasts indicators. Stylistic/terminology concern without a material change of tool identity.

plain_language_analysis: Elinikää lyhentäviä terveydentiloja is heavy but plain enough. Are less well is rendered as a clinical-status perfect (terveydentila on heikentynyt) rather than the source's plain current state (voivat huonommin).
terminology_analysis: Life shortening health conditions is preserved and not collapsed into end-of-life or terminal language. Terveydentila is slightly more formal than health/being less well.
semantic_risk_analysis: Less well is a present poorer state; on heikentynyt adds a completed deterioration. Look for as etsimään is acceptable for case-finding. A plan for care in the future is adequately suunnitelman tulevasta hoidosta.
backtranslation_signal: BT whose health has deteriorated restates the perfect-tense shift already present in Finnish; it does not hide a further error.
proposed_fi_if_needed: SPICT auttaa meitä etsimään ihmisiä, joilla on elinikää lyhentäviä terveydentiloja ja jotka voivat huonommin. Nämä ihmiset tarvitsevat nyt enemmän apua ja hoitoa sekä suunnitelman tulevasta hoidosta.
rationale: Core case-finding meaning is kept, but less well is recast as deteriorated health status. Unlikely to change who is identified, still worth a plain-language check.

plain_language_analysis: Clear question. Huonosta terveydentilasta is a little more formal than poor health, but merkkejä and pahenevat are ordinary Finnish.
terminology_analysis: Signs, poor health and health problems that are getting worse keep the same referents. Jotka pahenevat attaches to terveysongelmia, matching the English relative-clause scope.
semantic_risk_analysis: Question form, disjunction or, and worsening as process are preserved. No added diagnosis.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches the source closely; no hidden Finnish error.

plain_language_analysis: Sairaalaan otto(t) copies the English (s) plural mark and is healthcare jargon. Ordinary users more readily understand sairaalaan ottaminen, sairaalajaksot or päivystyskäynnit.
terminology_analysis: Kiireellinen vs päivystyksellinen reasonably splits urgent vs emergency. Käynnit is as underspecified as visits (ED vs any hospital visit).
semantic_risk_analysis: Admission versus visit and urgent versus emergency are not reversed. The (t) does not add a new clinical meaning.
backtranslation_signal: BT restores the English source wording and therefore does not reveal how un-Finnish otto(t) is.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Kiireellinen tai päivystyksellinen sairaalaan ottaminen tai käynnit.
rationale: Meaning is recoverable, but the parenthetical plural is a literal English device and otto is not plain Finnish.

plain_language_analysis: Toimintakyky is more technical than less able to manage. Tavanomaisissa toimissa is acceptable; vointi ei ole yhtä hyvä kuin ennen is good plain Finnish for not as well as they used to be.
terminology_analysis: Functioning is an ICF-style recast of ability to manage usual activities, not a different disease. Vuoteessa tai tuolissa matches bed or chair.
semantic_risk_analysis: Person-level agency (less able) becomes an abstract functioning decline. Time comparison to earlier state is kept in the second clause. Often and more than half the day are kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT functioning has declined confirms the agency abstraction; it does not hide a further error.
proposed_fi_if_needed:
Pystyy huonommin hoitamaan tavanomaisia toimia; vointi ei ole yhtä hyvä kuin ennen.
(Henkilö viettää usein yli puolet päivästä vuoteessa tai tuolissa.)
rationale: Sense is close, but the person is no longer the grammatical agent of being less able. Same pattern as S4A-2026-014.

plain_language_analysis: The genitive chain is heavy but readable. Needs more help and care from others is preserved in ordinary Finnish.
terminology_analysis: Physical and/or mental health problems is rendered as fyysisen terveyden ja/tai mielenterveyden ongelmien. Mielenterveys is the standard equivalent, not a new diagnosis.
semantic_risk_analysis: Increasing remains on the problems. From others and due to are kept. No modality change.
backtranslation_signal: BT aligns with the source. No hidden Finnish error.

plain_language_analysis: Henkilöstä huolehtiva ihminen is plain and avoids legal omaishoitaja, which would narrow the English carer.
terminology_analysis: Carer is treated as an informal caring person, not staff. That matches usual SPICT-4ALL carer use. The Finnish term is not project-approved, but the referent is not obviously wrong.
semantic_risk_analysis: Need is still on the carer, not the patient. More help and support preserved.
backtranslation_signal: BT the person who cares for them matches the Finnish paraphrase and the source role.

plain_language_analysis: On selvästi laihtunut and pysyy liian laihana are natural Finnish for clearly lost weight and stays too thin.
terminology_analysis: No disease label added. Thinness is not recast as cachexia or malnutrition.
semantic_risk_analysis: Over the last few months and the or stays too thin alternative are preserved. Clearly remains a degree marker.
backtranslation_signal: BT remains too thin matches stays too thin. No hidden error.

plain_language_analysis: Hankalia oireita and suurimman osan ajasta are good plain Finnish. Hänellä on is an added explicit subject in a list that is otherwise telegraphic.
terminology_analysis: Despite good treatment of their health problems becomes although those problems are treated well. Hoidetaan hyvin can mean treated kindly / well looked after, not necessarily adequate treatment of the conditions.
semantic_risk_analysis: The concessive despite is kept, but the quality-of-treatment meaning is ambiguous. Troublesome and most of the time are intact.
backtranslation_signal: BT treated well reproduces the Finnish ambiguity rather than restoring good treatment of the conditions. It can hide the false-friend reading.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Hankalia oireita suurimman osan ajasta huolimatta terveysongelmien hyvästä hoidosta.
rationale: Possible shift from adequate treatment of the problems to being treated well. Needs human check; not a proven reversal.

plain_language_analysis: Pyytää palliatiivista hoitoa is clear. Valitsee hoidon ... ottamatta jättämisen is stiff nominal style. Toivoo keskittymistä elämänlaatuun reduces the person's wish to focus into a hope for focusing.
terminology_analysis: Not have treatment is recast as ottamatta jättäminen, which in Finnish often sounds like not taking (a medicine) rather than declining or not receiving treatment. Palliatiivista hoitoa and elämänlaatuun are expected equivalents, not project-approved terms.
semantic_risk_analysis: Asks for / chooses / wishes remain person-or-family acts. Reduce and stop are kept. Not have vs not take is the material risk. Quality of life is not replaced by comfort or dying.
backtranslation_signal: BT not take treatment confirms the take/have shift. Diagnostic of the Finnish verb ottaa, not a BT artefact.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Henkilö (tai perhe) pyytää palliatiivista hoitoa; valitsee hoidon vähentämisen, lopettamisen tai sen, ettei hoitoa oteta; tai haluaa keskittyä elämänlaatuun.
rationale: Choice agency is kept, but not have treatment is liable to be read as not taking treatment. Agency on wishes to focus is also weakened.

plain_language_analysis: Natural checklist question. Jokin näistä is the ordinary Finnish for any of these.
terminology_analysis: Health problems remains terveysongelmista, consistent with nearby headings.
semantic_risk_analysis: Any as one-or-more is the normal reading of jokin näistä. No added restriction to a single problem only.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches the source.

plain_language_analysis: Syöpä is the ordinary Finnish heading.
terminology_analysis: Cancer is not narrowed to a tumour type or to malignancy jargon (pahanlaatuinen kasvain).
semantic_risk_analysis: No qualifier added or removed.
backtranslation_signal: BT Cancer matches.

plain_language_analysis: Sydämen tai verenkierron ongelmat is plain and parallel to the English heading.
terminology_analysis: Circulation as verenkierto is the right system referent, not pulse or blood pressure alone.
semantic_risk_analysis: Or is kept. Problems is not upgraded to disease.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches the source.

plain_language_analysis: Munuaisongelmat is a transparent compound at the same plainness as Kidney problems.
terminology_analysis: Kidney, not bladder or urinary tract. Consistent with later munuaiset / dialyysi units.
semantic_risk_analysis: No severity or chronicity added.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Same toimintakyky recast as S4A-2026-004. Terveys heikkenee is good plain Finnish for health is getting poorer.
terminology_analysis: Usual activities and health remain distinct. No disease name added.
semantic_risk_analysis: Less able becomes a completed functioning decline; getting poorer is correctly present-tense heikkenee. Cross-unit wording is consistent with 004.
backtranslation_signal: BT functioning has declined / health is deteriorating tracks the Finnish, including the agency shift.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Pystyy huonommin hoitamaan tavanomaisia toimia, ja terveys heikkenee.
rationale: Second clause is faithful; first clause repeats the 004 agency/plain-language issue.

plain_language_analysis: Sydämen vajaatoiminta is the common name for heart failure, slightly clinical but matching the source term. Hengenahdistusta / rintakipua are ordinary.
terminology_analysis: Heart blood vessel disease as sydämen verisuonisairaus stays at the source's plain specificity and does not insert sepelvaltimotauti.
semantic_risk_analysis: When resting, moving or walking a few steps is kept; muutaman askeleen attaches to walking, as in English.
backtranslation_signal: BT disease of the heart's blood vessels is a fair return of the Finnish, not a new error.

plain_language_analysis: Munuaiset eivät toimi hyvin is the right plain register for kidneys are not working well.
terminology_analysis: Not upgraded to kidney failure or uraemia. Yleinen terveys matches general health.
semantic_risk_analysis: Getting poorer as heikkenee is present-process, not a completed decline.
backtranslation_signal: BT deteriorating is a near synonym of getting poorer, not evidence of extra Finnish meaning.

plain_language_analysis: Hyväkuntoinen in everyday Finnish often means physically fit, not well enough in health to undergo cancer treatment. Riittävän hyvässä kunnossa would keep kunto in the clinical-condition sense more clearly.
terminology_analysis: Cancer treatment as syöpähoitoon is right. Treatment is to help with symptoms is kept as symptom-directed treatment, without naming palliation as a diagnosis.
semantic_risk_analysis: Not well enough is the key threshold. A fitness reading would change who is flagged. The or-branch about symptom-directed treatment is otherwise intact, if slightly telegraphic.
backtranslation_signal: BT is not well enough smooths hyväkuntoinen back into the English idiom and can hide the fitness false friend.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Ei ole riittävän hyvässä kunnossa syöpähoitoon, tai hoito on oireiden helpottamiseksi.
rationale: Fluent Finnish that ordinary users may hear as fitness rather than insufficient health for cancer treatment.

plain_language_analysis: Jalkaongelmia is understandable but jalka commonly means foot as well as leg. Jalkojen ongelmia would point more clearly to the limbs.
terminology_analysis: Poor blood circulation as huonon verenkierron is correct. Surgery is not possible keeps impossibility (ei ole mahdollinen), not preference.
semantic_risk_analysis: Due to causality is kept. No added ischaemia or amputation. Foot-versus-leg is the only referent risk.
backtranslation_signal: BT leg problems conceals the Finnish jalka ambiguity by restoring the English word.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Jalkojen ongelmia huonon verenkierron vuoksi; leikkaus ei ole mahdollinen.
rationale: Impossibility and circulation cause are faithful; jalka is a mild limb/foot ambiguity.

plain_language_analysis: Clear alternatives. Munuaisdialyysin then dialyysin in the same unit is slightly uneven but still plain.
terminology_analysis: Stopping dialysis versus choosing palliative care instead of starting dialysis are both present. Dialysis is not renamed hemodialyysi only.
semantic_risk_analysis: Choice agency on the second branch is kept. Instead of starting is not recast as stopping. No cannot/must shift.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches the source.

plain_language_analysis: Lopettaminen tai aloittamatta jättäminen is natural Finnish for stopping or not starting.
terminology_analysis: Dialysis referent is the same as 019. Not starting is not turned into refusing or being ineligible.
semantic_risk_analysis: Both alternatives remain possible actions, not impossibility.
backtranslation_signal: BT stopping dialysis or not starting it matches.

plain_language_analysis: Dementia is the common Finnish word. Standalone hauraus is odd for a person: it is the word for brittleness/fragility of objects and is unlikely to convey geriatric frailty to ordinary users.
terminology_analysis: Frailty is a specific health concept used with dementia. Hauraus without heikkous/raihnaus/oireyhtymä is incomplete as a heading and may be mistaken for brittle bones or general fragility, not the source concept.
semantic_risk_analysis: Or is kept. No false diagnosis such as osteoporosis is asserted, but the frailty heading may not be recognised.
backtranslation_signal: BT frailty restores the English technical term and hides how opaque hauraus is to a Finnish reader.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Dementia tai hauraus ja heikkous
rationale: Heading may fail as patient-facing frailty language. Terminology needs human review; this is not an adjudication of the clinical label.

plain_language_analysis: Hengitysongelmat is the right plain register for a 4ALL heading.
terminology_analysis: Respiratory problems is slightly more system-level than breathing problems. Finnish uses the same hengitys-word later for breathing problems (045), which is acceptable plain-language levelling, not a wrong organ system.
semantic_risk_analysis: Heading still covers lung/breathing illness. Not narrowed to asthma or COPD.
backtranslation_signal: BT breathing problems is expected from hengitys and does not prove a Finnish error.

plain_language_analysis: Maksaongelmat matches the source heading in form and plainness.
terminology_analysis: Liver, not gallbladder or pancreas. Consistent with 026–031.
semantic_risk_analysis: No chronicity or failure added.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Ei pysty ... ilman apua is natural Finnish for unable to ... without help.
terminology_analysis: Dress, walk and eat are the same three activities. Help is not upgraded to hoitaja or laitoshoito.
semantic_risk_analysis: Inability without help is preserved; not recast as unwillingness.
backtranslation_signal: BT cannot is the normal return of ei pysty, not a modality error in Finnish.

plain_language_analysis: Vointi on huonompi is good for more unwell. Yhteydessä is woolly for with (having) long-term lung problems. Kun rintakehä on parhaimmillaan is grammatically Finnish but semantically odd: rintakehä is the rib cage/thorax, which is not said to be at its best in ordinary Finnish.
terminology_analysis: Chest is at its best is an English respiratory idiom meaning when breathing/lungs are as good as they get, not during an exacerbation. Literal rintakehä points at anatomy, not baseline breathing. Long term lung problems as pitkäaikaisten keuhko-ongelmien is otherwise right.
semantic_risk_analysis: The baseline-versus-exacerbation contrast is likely lost or misunderstood. Short of breath when resting, moving or walking a few steps is otherwise intact.
backtranslation_signal: BT repeats the English idiom and records uncertainty. That flags the calque; it does not restore a correct Finnish meaning.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Vointi on huonompi pitkäaikaisten keuhko-ongelmien kanssa. Hengenahdistusta levätessä, liikkuessa tai kävellessä muutaman askeleen silloinkin, kun hengitys on parhaimmillaan.
rationale: Literal English-idiom translation that ordinary users can misread. Probable material error in the baseline-breathing clause.

plain_language_analysis: Kuluneen vuoden aikana pahentuneita is clear for worsening ... in the past year. Lisäongelmia is plainer than komplikaatioita but also vaguer.
terminology_analysis: Complications is a specific medical relation (sequelae of liver disease). Lisäongelmia broadens to any additional problems. The following list partly constrains the meaning.
semantic_risk_analysis: Past-year time window and worsening are kept. With is joinin liittyy, which is association rather than named complications. No negation change.
backtranslation_signal: BT additional problems confirms the broadening; it does not hide it.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Kuluneen vuoden aikana pahentuneita maksaongelmia, joihin liittyy liitännäisongelmia, kuten:
rationale: Time and worsening are faithful; complications is softened into extra problems and needs review.

plain_language_analysis: Nesteen kertymistä vatsaan matches belly rather than a technical ascites label.
terminology_analysis: Vatsa is the plain Finnish for belly. It can also mean the stomach organ, but with fluid building up the belly reading is the ordinary one. Not narrowed to vatsaontelo jargon.
semantic_risk_analysis: Process of building up / accumulation is kept. No cause added.
backtranslation_signal: BT abdomen is a register upgrade in the BT, not evidence that Finnish said abdomen.

plain_language_analysis: Ajoittaista sekavuutta is ordinary Finnish for being confused at times.
terminology_analysis: Sekavuus is the plain word for confused, not upgraded to delirium or encephalopathy, which the source does not name.
semantic_risk_analysis: At times as ajoittaista keeps intermittency without making it a formal periodic diagnosis. Nominal style matches the list.
backtranslation_signal: BT occasional confusion is a fair return.

plain_language_analysis: Same plain clause as 016, appropriate in a complications list.
terminology_analysis: Kidneys not working well is not escalated to failure. Consistent with 016.
semantic_risk_analysis: No time or degree added.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Infektioita is a common loanword here; tulehduksia would risk inflammation rather than infection.
terminology_analysis: Infections remains infections, not sepsis. Partitive infektioita fits the list.
semantic_risk_analysis: No frequency added (unlike 038's frequent).
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Ruokatorvi is the ordinary Finnish for gullet/oesophagus, not overly specialist in this context.
terminology_analysis: Gullet is oesophagus, not throat (nielu/kurkku) and not stomach. Verenvuotoa ruokatorvesta keeps the bleeding-from relation.
semantic_risk_analysis: From the gullet is not broadened to any GI bleed.
backtranslation_signal: BT oesophagus is the expected return of ruokatorvi and does not indicate a Finnish error versus gullet.

plain_language_analysis: Syö ja juo vähemmän is more natural than a gerund and matches the source meaning. Nielemisvaikeuksia is the common word for difficulty with swallowing.
terminology_analysis: Eating, drinking and swallowing remain separate. Not recast as aspiration or dysphagia loanword.
semantic_risk_analysis: Less is comparative quantity, not inability (that is 024). Semicolon list structure kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Tarvitsee käyttää is a stiff calque of needs to use. Natural Finnish is joutuu käyttämään or tarvitsee happea ... . Meaning stays clear.
terminology_analysis: Oxygen as happea is the plain therapy word, not happirikastin or NIV jargon. Much of the day and night as suuren osan päivästä ja yöstä is accurate.
semantic_risk_analysis: Need to use remains necessity of oxygen use, not mere benefit. Duration across day and night is kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT a large part of is a fair reading of suuren osan / much of.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Joutuu käyttämään happea suuren osan päivästä ja yöstä.
rationale: Unnatural verb pair without a likely meaning change.

plain_language_analysis: Virtsarakon ja suolen hallinta on heikkoa is a literal control calque. Ordinary Finnish for this meaning is pidätyskyky / ei pidätä virtsaa ja ulostetta.
terminology_analysis: Bladder and bowels are the continence referents, not urine infection or constipation. Hallinta is abstract next to the source's plain poor control.
semantic_risk_analysis: Poor remains degree. Both bladder and bowel are present. Has is implied in the list style.
backtranslation_signal: BT bladder and bowel control is poor tracks the calque and therefore does not expose the un-Finnish hallinta.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Virtsan ja suolen pidätyskyky on heikko.
rationale: Sense of incontinence is recoverable, but the wording is a literal English control metaphor.

plain_language_analysis: Hengityskone is the ordinary Finnish for a breathing machine, not a more technical ventilaattori.
terminology_analysis: Breathing machine is not upgraded to a named ventilator mode. In hospital as sairaalassa is kept. Hengityskone may be pictured as an ICU machine, which is close to the source's hospital breathing machine.
semantic_risk_analysis: Has needed is past need (on tarvinnut), not current use only. Treatment with is kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT ventilator is BT register, not extra specificity in the Finnish.

plain_language_analysis: Ei pysty viestimään puhumalla is understandable, if a little formal (viestiä). Ei vastaa juurikaan muihin ihmisiin uses the wrong complement: vastata + illative with people is odd Finnish (sounds like answer into people). Natural is vastaa muille ihmisille or ei reagoi muihin ihmisiin.
terminology_analysis: Communicate by speaking is not reduced to mute/aphasia as a diagnosis. Responding is behavioural responsiveness, which reagoida would carry more clearly.
semantic_risk_analysis: Not able vs not responding much remain two clauses. Much as juurikaan is fair. Case government may cause a momentary wrong parse (match/correspond) but the intended unreadiness to respond is still guessable.
backtranslation_signal: BT responds very little to other people repairs the Finnish government and can hide how odd muihin ihmisiin is.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Ei pysty viestimään puhumalla; ei vastaa juurikaan muille ihmisille.
rationale: Second clause is fluent-looking but semantically odd Finnish; meaning is probably recoverable, still needs review.

plain_language_analysis: Toistuvia kaatumisia is ordinary for frequent/recurrent falls. Reisiluun murtuma matches the source's already anatomical femur.
terminology_analysis: Femur is not narrowed to lonkkamurtuma (hip fracture) and not broadened to any fracture.
semantic_risk_analysis: Frequent as toistuvia is recurrent, which is the screening sense. Semicolon list kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT repeated falls is a near synonym of frequent here.

plain_language_analysis: Toistuvia infektioita; keuhkokuume is plain and parallel to 037.
terminology_analysis: Pneumonia as keuhkokuume is the common Finnish word. Infections not narrowed to a pathogen.
semantic_risk_analysis: Frequent kept as toistuvia. Pneumonia is listed, not required as the only infection.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Hermoston ongelmat is clear and avoids hermo-ongelmat (nerves/nervousness).
terminology_analysis: Nervous system is hermosto, not mental health and not peripheral nerve pain alone.
semantic_risk_analysis: Heading is not turned into a named neurological diagnosis.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches.

plain_language_analysis: Muut terveydentilat is readable. Terveydentila in Finnish often means health status rather than a disease grouping.
terminology_analysis: Source says other conditions, not other health conditions. Adding terveys- is a small explicitness addition. Compared with 042, terveydentila is used both for conditions and for status, which is slightly blurry.
semantic_risk_analysis: Other is kept. No condition is invented. The heading still points at remaining illnesses.
backtranslation_signal: BT other health conditions shows the added health; it does not hide a worse error.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Muut sairaudet tai tilat
rationale: Minor broadening/explicitness, not a likely mis-grouping of the section.

plain_language_analysis: Fyysinen terveys ja mielenterveys heikkenevät is plain and parallel.
terminology_analysis: Mental health as mielenterveys matches 005/047. Not turned into psychiatric diagnosis.
semantic_risk_analysis: Both domains and getting worse as present heikkenevät are kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT deteriorating is a synonym of getting worse, not extra Finnish meaning.

plain_language_analysis: Long but readable. Less well again becomes terveydentila on heikentynyt (see 001). Ei tehoa hyvin is slightly drug-efficacy language for will not work well; ei toimi hyvin would be plainer and closer.
terminology_analysis: Physical or mental illnesses or health conditions becomes three listed types, with mielenterveyden sairauksia for mental illnesses. Other and life shortening are kept and not collapsed to terminal.
semantic_risk_analysis: Less well with is split into deteriorated health AND having those illnesses, which makes two checks more explicit than the English with. No treatment available is faithful. Will not work well is present-tense ei tehoa hyvin (general ineffectiveness rather than predicted failure).
backtranslation_signal: BT does not work well / health has deteriorated reflects the Finnish tense and less-well recast.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Ihmiset, jotka voivat huonommin ja joilla on muita elinikää lyhentäviä fyysisiä sairauksia, mielenterveyden sairauksia tai terveydentiloja. Hoitoa ei ole saatavilla tai se ei toimi hyvin.
rationale: Availability/ineffectiveness contrast is kept; less well and work well are slightly recast. Same less-well pattern as 001.

plain_language_analysis: Enemmän ongelmia puhumisessa ja viestimisessä is clear. Nieleminen vaikeutuu is natural Finnish.
terminology_analysis: Speaking and communicating stay distinct from 036's not able to communicate by speaking. Swallowing is not named dysfagia.
semantic_risk_analysis: More problems is comparative frequency/amount. Swallowing is getting worse is general deterioration; vaikeutuu specifies becoming more difficult, which may miss other worsening (choking, safer textures) but is close.
backtranslation_signal: BT becomes more difficult confirms the specification to difficulty.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Enemmän ongelmia puhumisessa ja viestimisessä; nieleminen heikkenee.
rationale: Speaking/communicating is faithful; swallowing worsening is slightly narrowed to difficulty.

plain_language_analysis: Mitä voimme tehdä ... auttamiseksi is a normal Finnish heading, a little bureaucratic in the auttamiseksi noun, but clear.
terminology_analysis: Person and family are both kept. We remains the tool users.
semantic_risk_analysis: English is a heading, not a question; Finnish Mitä without a question mark is also a heading. BT's question form is a BT reading, not a Finnish interrogative marker.
backtranslation_signal: BT what can we do adds question force the Finnish heading does not mark. Do not treat that as a Finnish error.

plain_language_analysis: Rintakehän infektioita is not an established Finnish expression for the UK plain term chest infections. It sounds like infection of the thorax/chest wall. Keuhkokuume and hengitysongelmia are otherwise ordinary.
terminology_analysis: Chest infection in the source is a lower-respiratory/lung infection, listed beside pneumonia. Rintakehä is the anatomical chest. Cross-unit: 025 also translates chest literally as rintakehä. Breathing problems as hengitysongelmia is fine and consistent with 022.
semantic_risk_analysis: Pairing with pneumonia helps a reader guess lungs, but the head term can still misdirect to chest-wall/thoracic infection. Not a modality error.
backtranslation_signal: BT chest infections restores the English idiom from rintakehän infektioita and thereby hides the Finnish anatomical calque.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Keuhkoinfektioita tai keuhkokuume; hengitysongelmia.
rationale: Literal chest calque with a clinically plausible wrong referent. Back-translation conceals it. Probable material error.

plain_language_analysis: Aloita keskustelu is a shade more formal than start talking, but the instruction is clear. Siltä varalta, että asiat muuttuvat is excellent for in case things change.
terminology_analysis: Family or carer matches 006 (hänestä huolehtivan ihmisen). Help needed now is not turned into services jargon.
semantic_risk_analysis: Imperative to the user, person+family/carer addressees, now vs plans if things change are all kept. Why making plans is important is kept.
backtranslation_signal: BT matches closely.

plain_language_analysis: Toimintarajoite is official/ICF Finnish, not everyday language for disability. Jatkuva and yhden tai useamman aivohalvauksen jälkeen are clear.
terminology_analysis: Disability is not narrowed to a legal vamma status, but toimintarajoite may still be opaque. Stroke as aivohalvaus is the common term. Physical and/or mental health problems matches 005.
semantic_risk_analysis: Ongoing, increasing, and after one or more strokes are present. With as johon liittyy keeps the disability-plus-problems relation. After attaches at the end, with similar English attachment ambiguity.
backtranslation_signal: BT functional limitation reflects toimintarajoite and does not hide a worse shift.
proposed_fi_if_needed: Jatkuva toimintakyvyn rajoite, johon liittyy lisääntyviä fyysisen terveyden ja/tai mielenterveyden ongelmia yhden tai useamman aivohalvauksen jälkeen.
